xindi-zhang.title: The tool that expands my art: Xindi Zhang's Oscar-shortlisted thesis, built in ComfyUI
xindi-zhang.description: How a USC Expanded Animation thesis became a Student Academy Award winner, an Oscar shortlist entry, and helped land a job at Amazon — with the artist's own illustrations as the style guide.

topic-1.body:
<Section id="topic-1">

<Embed src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/1131160045" title="The Song of Drifters by Xindi Zhang" />

*From The Song of Drifters. Film images: Xindi Zhang.*

### Tell us about The Song of Drifters. What is it about, and where did it start?

The Song of Drifters is a documentary animation about people caught between leaving and returning, wanderers who drift through unfamiliar cities, holding onto memories of a homeland out of reach and searching for a sense of belonging. The title is a direct translation from an ancient Chinese poem about a mother's love for a child who leaves her hometown. My version takes the opposite point of view, from the child's perspective.

I built the film in ComfyUI. When I started, I was not trying to show what AI could do. I was trying to prove something almost opposite.

<Quote>It started as a challenge to the stereotype that AI-generated work is generic and cheap. I wanted to prove that AI could be an amplifier for personal vision, not a replacement for it.</Quote>

</Section>
topic-1.label: INTRO

topic-2.body:
<Section id="topic-2">

### You came to this from illustration, not engineering. How did you end up in ComfyUI?

I started as an illustrator. I earned my BFA in illustration at the Rhode Island School of Design, then worked as a game concept artist, where I picked up shaders, Unity, and Unreal. That technical side made me a fast learner with new tools. Later I went to USC's School of Cinematic Arts for an MFA in Expanded Animation, where I studied with Professor Kathy Smith.

By my thesis year I had moved from Stable Diffusion's standard interfaces to ComfyUI, because I think in node-based structures and I wanted to control every step. Most AI tools are one click: you prompt, you click, you get a result. That is not what I wanted.

<Quote>I want to control the process, and the process is even more important than the result itself. For artists like me, I don't want to automate anything. I want to participate in every single stage of designing the workflow. That's the fun part of it.</Quote>

</Section>
topic-2.label: WHY COMFYUI

topic-3.body: ### Walk us through the pipeline. What were you actually feeding the model? My core technique was style transfer in Stable Diffusion 1.5, driven by IP-Adapter and ControlNet. What mattered most was what I fed it: my own work. The base materials were live-action footage I shot on an iPhone 15 Pro and 3D animation I built in Blender. The AI restyled imagery I had already made. It did not invent it. Unlike most AI-generated videos, which use other artists' works from the model, I use my own illustrations as the style guide. I also trained custom LoRAs on my own video, footage of the cities I had lived in. Capturing that footage became a vital part of the documentary process. Wandering through the streets where I once lived let me reconnect with those cities. Most of it never appears in the final cut, but it lives in the visuals as training data. The hybrid pipeline made rendering the final look more efficient and saved more time for ideation. For the dream sequences I combined animated 3D with AI morphing, moving from abstract to concrete to mimic the feeling of being half awake.
topic-3.label: THE PIPELINE

topic-5.body:
<Section id="topic-5">

### The film won gold at the Student Academy Awards and was shortlisted for the Oscars. What's next?

I made the film for creative reasons, not career ones. I honestly did not expect it to connect to a job at all. Then it won the Golden Award at the 2025 Student Academy Awards and was shortlisted for the Oscars, and the calls started.

<Figure src="https://media.comfy.org/website/customers/xindi-zhang/awards.png" alt="Xindi Zhang at the 2025 Student Academy Awards" caption="Xindi Zhang at the 2025 Student Academy Awards. Source: Oscars Press Office." />

What people wanted was the combination: someone who understands both traditional craft and AI tools. I now work as an AI Creative at Amazon AI Studio building custom production pipelines. I see that same demand across the industry, with ComfyUI experience starting to show up as a requirement in job postings at major studios and design agencies.

<Quote>It's not the tool that steals my art. It's the tool that expands my art.</Quote>

My advice to other students is not really about software. AI is just another tool to convey ideas, but nothing is more important than the story itself. If you use AI, use it on purpose. The more you understand it, the more freedom you have to make work that is genuinely yours.

</Section>

change-cancel-plan-refunds.question: Can I change or cancel my plan? Do you offer refunds?
change-cancel-plan-refunds.body: You can cancel any time. Cancelling stops all future payments immediately, and your plan stays active until the end of the period you've already paid for. For refunds, submit a support ticket. These are reviewed by our team case by case.

commercial-model-licenses.question: Do you offer commercial licenses for open-weight models like MiniMax H3?
commercial-model-licenses.body: Yes. Licenses come in two tiers, Professional and Enterprise. See the [MiniMax Commercial License page](/minimax/license), or [contact sales](/contact) to request one.

difference-between-plans.question: What's the difference between Standard, Creator, and Pro?
difference-between-plans.body:
**Standard -** 30-min max runtime per workflow, 1 concurrent workflow via API. For individuals building workflows.

**Creator -** Everything in Standard plus the ability to **import your own models** (from CivitAI or Hugging Face) and run up to 3 workflows concurrently via API.

**Pro -** Everything in Creator plus **longer runtime (up to 1 hour)** per workflow and up to 5 concurrent workflows via API. For teams running Comfy in production.

do-credits-roll-over.question: Do unused credits roll over?
do-credits-roll-over.body: Plan credits reset at the end of each billing cycle and don't roll over — monthly on monthly plans, and once a year on annual plans, which receive their whole year of credits up front. **Top-up credits do persist.** They're valid for a year and aren't affected by your plan's reset. Credits work on Comfy Cloud, and on Comfy Desktop **only when calling Partner Nodes.** Comfy Desktop itself is free.

find-invoices-tax-id.question: Where can I find my invoices or add my company's tax ID?
find-invoices-tax-id.body: You can manage all billing details directly through your Stripe portal. Go to Settings → Plans & Credits → Invoice History to open it. From there, you can view and download invoices, update your billing information, and add your company's tax ID.

how-does-pricing-work.question: How does Comfy Cloud pricing actually work?
how-does-pricing-work.body: Every plan includes a pool of **credits** — refilled each month on monthly plans, granted for the whole year up front on annual plans. Credits are spent on two things: **active GPU time** while a workflow is running, and **Partner Nodes** (proprietary models like Nano Banana Pro). You're never charged for idle time. Building or editing a workflow costs nothing. You only spend while a job is actually running.

how-does-team-plan-work.question: How does the Team Plan work?
how-does-team-plan-work.body:
The Team Plan puts your whole team on **one shared credit pool.** Every member draws from the same balance, so you're not juggling separate subscriptions. Key things to know:

**One pool, shared.** Everyone generates against the same credit balance.

**Invite by email.** Add teammates, and resend or revoke access any time.

**Owners manage billing.** Assign owners who handle payment and buy top-ups for the team.

**Upgrade in place.** Move an existing workspace to a team and your workflows, models, and assets stay attached.

Choose your monthly credit commitment that fits your team. [Get started today.](https://cloud.comfy.org/?pricing=team)

partner-nodes-cost.question: What are Partner Nodes, and do they cost extra?
partner-nodes-cost.body: Partner Nodes let you run proprietary models (like Nano Banana Pro) directly inside your workflow. They draw from the same credit pool as your subscription (no separate bill); how much each call costs depends on the model and parameters you set. These credits work across both Comfy Cloud and Comfy Desktop. [Read more about Partner Nodes](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/partner-nodes/overview).

run-out-of-credits.question: What happens when I run out of credits?
run-out-of-credits.body: You can buy **top-up credits** at any time without changing plans. Plan credits are spent first; top-ups are only drawn down once your plan allowance is used up. Top-up credits stay valid for **1 year** from purchase.

run-workflows-via-api.question: Can I run workflows via API?
run-workflows-via-api.body: Yes. Run Comfy workflows programmatically via API. Concurrency limits scale with your plan: 1 / 3 / 5 on Standard / Creator / Pro. It's built for integrating ComfyUI into your apps, automating batch jobs, or running production pipelines. If you need to request increasing limits you can do so [here](https://comfysupport.portal.usepylon.com/forms/team-plan-requests).

running-comfy-at-scale.question: What if I'm running Comfy at scale?
running-comfy-at-scale.body: For teams running Comfy in production and at scale, Enterprise adds higher API rate limits, advanced security, and dedicated support. [Learn more about Enterprise](https://comfy.org/enterprise/) or reach out at [enterprise@comfy.org](mailto:enterprise@comfy.org).

runtime-and-concurrency-limits.question: What are the runtime and concurrency limits?
runtime-and-concurrency-limits.body: Each workflow has a max runtime of **30 minutes** on Standard and Creator, raised to **1 hour** on Pro. Jobs over the limit are cancelled automatically to keep the system fair and stable. You can queue up to **100 workflows** at once, and run **1 / 3 / 5** concurrently via API on Standard / Creator / Pro. If you need to increase your Team plan concurrency limit, seats or API rate limits, contact us [here](https://comfysupport.portal.usepylon.com/forms/team-plan-requests).

team-collaboration-features.question: What collaboration features are included at launch?
team-collaboration-features.body: At launch, a Team plan gives you **shared infrastructure**: one credit pool, one bill, one set of admins. **Workflow and asset sharing inside the workspace is coming soon.** In the meantime, to hand off, share the workflow, export the workflow JSON, or drop a Comfy-generated asset into another canvas.

team-concurrency.question: How does concurrency work on a Team plan? Can multiple members run workflows at the same time?
team-concurrency.body: Yes. On a Team plan, the workspace has a greater concurrency limit per member than the Pro plan. If you run into issues you can request additional support for your team plan limits [here](https://comfysupport.portal.usepylon.com/forms/team-plan-requests).

team-per-seat-pricing.question: Is Team pricing per-seat? Can I add a freelancer just for a project?
team-per-seat-pricing.body: No. Team pricing is based on **your monthly credit commit**, not per-seat. Invite a freelancer, they draw from the shared credit pool while they're working, then remove them when the project wraps. **No charge for adding or removing people.** Member count is capped at **50** today; if you hit the cap, [contact support](https://portal.usepylon.com/comfy-org/forms/question) for additional seats.

team-spending-controls.question: Can I control how my team spends credits?
team-spending-controls.body: Today, owners control the shared pool and top-ups. We're actively building finer-grained controls: **spending limits** at the user, project, and workspace level, **per-project budgets and chargebacks**, **auto-recharge** when the pool runs low, and **self-serve teams beyond 50 seats**.

team-tier-pricing.question: What do the Team plan tiers cost, and how does the discount work?
team-tier-pricing.body: Team plans come in **five tiers from $200 to $2,500/month**, set by a credit-commit slider. A bigger monthly commit means a bigger discount: **annual plans go up to 20% off, monthly plans up to 10%**. The discount starts at the $400 tier (5% annual / 2.5% monthly) and scales from there.

team-upgrade-carryover.question: What carries over when I upgrade my workspace to a Team plan?
team-upgrade-carryover.body: Everything stays. You're upgrading the workspace itself, so **workflows, models, run history, and top-up credits all remain attached**. The only exception: unused credits from your old plan expire at the end of your current billing cycle, since you're moving to a new credit allowance. **Top-up credits carry over.**

what-is-a-credit-worth.question: What's a credit worth? How far does it go?
what-is-a-credit-worth.body:
Credits map to GPU runtime, so mileage depends on the workflow. As a reference point, a five-second video* uses roughly **11 credits**, so Standard covers a few hundred per month, Creator about double that, and Pro enough for over a thousand.

\*Based on 5s videos using the Wan 2.2 Image-to-Video template at default settings (81 frames, 18fps, 640×640, 4-step sampler). Heavier models, higher resolutions, and the inclusion of Partner nodes use more.

what-is-chatgpt-image-2-5.question: What is ChatGPT Images 2.5?
what-is-chatgpt-image-2-5.answer: ChatGPT Images 2.5 is an OpenAI image model for generating new visuals and editing existing images from natural-language instructions. In ComfyUI, it runs through Partner Nodes and can be combined with the rest of your workflow.

how-to-run.question: How do I run ChatGPT Images 2.5 in ComfyUI?
how-to-run.answer: Open [Comfy Cloud](https://cloud.comfy.org/?template=api_openai_gpt_image_25_flare_t2i&utm_source=comfy.org&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=gpt-image-2-5), add the OpenAI image Partner Node to a workflow, enter a prompt, and connect any reference images you want to use.

image-editing.question: Can ChatGPT Images 2.5 edit an existing image?
image-editing.answer: Yes. Supply an image and describe the change you want, from replacing objects and restyling a scene to focused masked edits. You can keep the result in the same graph for further processing.

reference-images.question: Can I use reference images?
reference-images.answer: Yes. Reference images can guide the subject, composition, materials, or visual language of a generation. Describe which qualities should carry into the result.

prompting.question: How should I prompt ChatGPT Images 2.5?
prompting.answer: Write a clear creative brief: name the subject, setting, composition, lighting, medium, and any text that must appear. For edits, state what should change and what must stay untouched.

comfy-workflows.question: Why use ChatGPT Images 2.5 in a ComfyUI workflow?
comfy-workflows.answer: The generated image becomes one step in a larger, repeatable pipeline. Route it into masking, compositing, upscaling, animation, or another model while keeping every step visible and adjustable.

prompt-syntax.question: Do I need special prompt syntax or keywords for Flux 3?
prompt-syntax.answer: No. Flux 3 interprets and rewrites your prompt before generation, so plain language works. Describe the scene the way you would brief a colleague. Keyword stacking and caption-style prose add nothing.

prompt-rewriting.question: Does Flux 3 change my prompt? Will it override what I asked for?
prompt-rewriting.answer: It rewrites, but the rewrite preserves what you explicitly specify. The more precisely you describe a scene, the more of the output is your call rather than the model's. Vague prompts hand control to the rewriter.

burned-in-text.question: Why is my text appearing burned into the video instead of being spoken?
burned-in-text.answer: Quoted text without a visible speaker tends to render as on-screen text. To get a spoken line: quote the line, describe a speaker visible on camera, and add "no on-screen text, no subtitles".

audio-control.question: How do I control audio in Flux 3?
audio-control.answer: Describe audio in layers and name each one separately: ambient sound, music, and speech. Each lands as its own layer. Lumping them into one phrase gives you less control over the mix.

multi-shot.question: Can Flux 3 generate multiple shots in one generation?
multi-shot.answer: Yes. Structure the prompt as "SHOT ONE ... HARD CUT. SHOT TWO ..." and it produces real cuts inside a single generation. For an uncut take, ask explicitly for "one continuous unbroken shot".

cuts-not-reading.question: Why do my cuts not look like cuts?
cuts-not-reading.answer: Consecutive shots that are too similar will not register as edits. Change scale, location, or colour between shots so the cut reads cleanly.

music-bed.question: Can I hold one music bed across multiple shots?
music-bed.answer: Yes. Specify it directly, such as "one continuous music bed across all three shots", alongside the shot structure.

prompt-examples.question: What does a good Flux 3 prompt look like?
prompt-examples.answer:
Three examples, copy and paste ready.

Plain brief: A cozy ramen shop on a rainy Tokyo night: steam rising from the broth, neon reflections in the window puddles, the cook working calmly. Rain patter and quiet kitchen sounds.

Spoken line: A weather presenter on camera in front of a stylized storm map, speaking directly to the lens: "Storm season is here and this time, we're ready." Confident delivery, clean studio lighting. No on-screen text, no subtitles.

Multi-shot: SHOT ONE: wide aerial of a desert highway at dawn, a single red car speeding through. HARD CUT. SHOT TWO: interior close-up, the driver's hands drumming the wheel to the radio. HARD CUT. SHOT THREE: from the roadside, the car shrinking into the heat haze. Warm engine hum under one continuous music bed across all three shots.

what-is-omni-flash.question: What is Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash?
what-is-omni-flash.answer: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is Google's multimodal video model, built for fast video generation, editing, and cinematic control. It processes text, image, audio, and video together, generates clips with an audio track, and edits existing video from plain-language instructions. It replaces earlier versions of Gemini Omni Flash.

extend-a-video.question: Can Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash extend a video?
extend-a-video.answer: Yes. With task type set to extend, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash reads the prior motion and composition of a clip and continues the shot, holding character identity and lighting steady. A prompt like "continue the shot: the woman finishes the violin solo and takes a bow" picks up where the clip ends.

commercial-use.question: Can I use Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash commercially?
commercial-use.answer: Yes. Output generated through ComfyUI partner nodes can be used in commercial work, subject to ComfyUI's terms and Google's usage policies. All videos carry a SynthID watermark, which is invisible to viewers but programmatically detectable for provenance.

resolutions-and-aspect-ratios.question: What resolutions and aspect ratios does Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash support in ComfyUI?
resolutions-and-aspect-ratios.answer: The Gemini Video Omni node outputs Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash video at 360p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K, in 16:9 or 9:16. Landscape is the default; set 9:16 for vertical clips. Higher resolutions take longer to generate.

edit-an-existing-video.question: Can Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash edit an existing video?
edit-an-existing-video.answer: Yes. Connect a clip to the node's video input and describe the change, and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash applies it while preserving everything else. Short prompts work best: "make this video anime," "change the lighting to be more dramatic." Add "keep everything else the same" when targeting a single element.

compared-to-previous-omni-flash.question: How does Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash compare to the previous Omni Flash?
compared-to-previous-omni-flash.answer: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is a full replacement for earlier Omni Flash versions, with the same generate-and-edit workflow and faster generation. The 1.1 release lets you draft videos more efficiently at 360p, upscale to 4K resolution, and extend scenes for longer storytelling.

cost-in-comfyui.question: How much does Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash cost in ComfyUI?
cost-in-comfyui.answer: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is billed per generation through ComfyUI credits, with cost varying by resolution. See the ComfyUI pricing page for current rates. No separate Google subscription is needed.

whats-new.question: What's new in LTX-2.5 vs LTX-2.3?

diffusion-fidelity-rendering.question: What is Diffusion Fidelity Rendering?
diffusion-fidelity-rendering.answer: The core change in this release. Instead of spending compute evenly across a scene, the model allocates it by complexity. Structure comes first: motion, composition, and framing generate in an 8x temporally compressed latent space, alongside a set of high-fidelity keyframes, more for complex scenes and fewer for simple ones. A dedicated pixel-diffusion stage then renders the final video from structure and keyframes together. Textures, materials, intricate objects, and faces resolve with pixel-level precision, and busy shots draw more rendering compute than static ones.

which-variant.question: Which LTX-2.5 variant should I use?

run-in-comfyui.question: How do I run LTX-2.5 in ComfyUI?

clip-length.question: How long can LTX-2.5 videos be?
clip-length.answer: Through Partner Nodes, Fast runs 2 to 20 seconds, with clips over 10 seconds capped at 720p or 1080p and 24 or 25 FPS. Pro runs 2 to 10 seconds. LTX-2.5 also ships an experimental duration head that reads the action in your prompt and sets clip length before diffusion starts.

native-audio.question: Does LTX-2.5 generate audio?
native-audio.answer: Yes. Synchronized audio and video carry over from LTX-2.3, and multi-shot generations hold voice across cuts.

multi-shot.question: Can LTX-2.5 generate more than one shot?
multi-shot.answer: Yes. One generation produces multiple connected shots, holding character, environment, lighting, voice, and style across the cuts. You get a sequence from a single run instead of matching separate generations afterward.

fine-tuning.question: Can I fine-tune LTX-2.5?
fine-tuning.answer: Yes. The base checkpoint is built for adaptation, so you can fine-tune the raw model on your own data.

native-audio.question: Does MiniMax H3 generate audio?

open-weights.question: Is MiniMax H3 available as Open Weights?
open-weights.answer: Yes. H3 is available as Open Weights, so you can run it yourself, and through Partner Nodes on Comfy Cloud. To use what you make locally for commercial work, [get an H3 commercial license through Comfy](https://comfy.org/minimax/license).

professional.description: A fixed-price monthly license for studios and teams shipping client work. Up to 10 licensed users, on distilled open-weight model versions.

who-needs-a-license.question: Who needs a MiniMax H3 commercial license?

whats-included.question: What does the license include?
whats-included.answer: Full commercial rights to your outputs: everything you generate is yours to use, sell, and ship. Fine-tuning and LoRA training on your characters, your style, or your product. Client and downstream work, so agencies and studios can use H3 for customer projects.

cloud-already-covered.question: I'm on Comfy Cloud. Do I need a license?
cloud-already-covered.answer: No. Comfy Cloud subscriptions already include commercial rights to what you generate. This license is for running H3 locally on your own hardware.

plans.question: What is the difference between the Professional and Enterprise tiers?
plans.answer: Professional is a fixed-price monthly license for studios and teams shipping client work, with up to 10 licensed users on distilled open-weight model versions. Enterprise is an annual agreement with custom volume pricing, no user cap, and every model version, undistilled weights included. Request a license and we will help you pick.

pricing-parity.question: Is the Commercial License more expensive through Comfy?
pricing-parity.answer: No. **MiniMax requires pricing parity across its Commercial License resellers**, so purchasing the license through Comfy does not come with a reseller markup or a higher license price compared with other authorized channels.

audio-music.question: Does the license cover MiniMax's audio and music models?
audio-music.answer: Yes. MiniMax commercial licenses through Comfy cover MiniMax H3 and MiniMax Audio & Music, available globally, so video, audio, and music sit under one agreement. MiniMax Music 3 has its own Community License that allows free commercial use below 20 million US dollars in yearly revenue; above that threshold, it needs a commercial license too.

not-covered.question: What is not covered?
not-covered.answer: Reselling or sublicensing the model, and running a model marketplace, API aggregator, inference-as-a-service, or model-routing platform. The license is for building your own products and content.

what-is-minimax-music-3.question: What is MiniMax Music 3?
what-is-minimax-music-3.answer: An open weights music generation model that writes complete songs. Give it lyrics and a description of the sound, and it returns a finished track with vocals and full arrangement.

how-to-use.question: How do I use MiniMax Music 3?

To use the model locally, download Comfy Desktop, create a new ComfyUI instance or update an existing one, search MiniMax Music 3 in the example workflows, download the models and run.

song-length.question: How long can MiniMax Music 3 songs be?
song-length.answer: Up to five minutes in a single generation. Structure holds across the full length, so melody, rhythm, and vocal identity stay consistent from intro to outro.

control-vocals.question: Can I control the vocals?
control-vocals.answer: Yes. You can set gender, timbre, performance style, harmony, backing vocals, and effects.

audio-quality.question: What audio quality does MiniMax Music 3 output?

free-to-use.question: Is MiniMax Music 3 free to use?
free-to-use.answer: Yes. MiniMax Music 3 is open weight under the [MiniMax Community License](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3/blob/main/LICENSE), free to use, including commercially, for companies under 20 million US dollars in yearly revenue.

commercial-use.question: Can I use MiniMax Music 3 commercially?
commercial-use.answer: Yes, for companies under 20 million US dollars in yearly revenue, under the MiniMax Community License. Above that threshold you need MiniMax authorization, which [a MiniMax commercial license through Comfy](https://comfy.org/minimax/license) covers.

image-editing.question: Can Qwen Image 2.1 edit an existing image?

clip-length.question: How long can Seedance 2.5 videos be?
clip-length.answer: Up to 30 seconds natively, and you can chain shots on the canvas when you need a longer cut.

native-audio.question: Does Seedance 2.5 generate audio?
native-audio.answer: Yes. Dialogue, music and sound effects are generated with the frame, so you do not have to score the clip afterwards.

is-it-free.question: Is Seedance 2.5 free to use?
is-it-free.answer: Seedance runs on pay-as-you-go or subscription credits. You can draft the same shot free on Wan 2.2 first, and spend credits only on the final render.

commercial-use.question: Can I use the videos commercially?
commercial-use.answer: Yes. Renders include commercial use and carry no watermark.

what-is-wan-3.question: What is Wan 3.0?
what-is-wan-3.answer: Alibaba's latest video model. Give it a prompt, up to 20 reference assets, or even a document and it generates up to 30 seconds with native audio.

whats-new.question: What's new in Wan 3.0 vs Wan 2.7?
whats-new.answer: Native 30-second clips, up to 20 reference inputs, and 480p generations for quick and cost effective generations.

prompting.question: How do I prompt Wan 3.0?
prompting.answer: Start simple: subject, scene, motion — one sentence is enough for a full clip. For more control, layer in camera movement, lighting, style, and sound, or address your uploads directly with @ syntax: "@Image1 walks through the door and says the line from @Audio1." The longer and more precise the prompt, the closer the output tracks your intent — it accepts up to 20,000 characters.

video-editing.question: Can Wan 3.0 edit video I already have?
video-editing.answer: Yes. Describe the change — remove an object, relight the scene, swap a subject — and everything else in the frame stays put. It can also extend existing footage.

clip-length.question: How long can clips be?
clip-length.answer: Anywhere from 2 to 30 seconds, generated in one continuous take — no stitching. Audio is generated natively, or switch it off.
